subject: LGCM: to constrain or not constrain residual covariances?

messages.author: 3245b266a5b20141
messages.subject: LGCM: to constrain or not constrain residual covariances?
parts:
Hi, all-

First post. I'm having a difficult time with my project, and nobody my committee who knows enough about growth curve modeling to help. The main question I'm grappling with is a conceptual one. I hope you can help.

I'm testing what's essentially a 3rd-order growth model (n = 275) across four time-points. It looks something like this:

x1 =~ item1 + item2 + item3
x2 =~ item4 + item5 + item6
x3 =~ item7 + item8 + item9

y =~ x1 + x2 + x3

I've tested the model for measurement invariance; it meets for strict invariance across all time-points.

However, while I am able to estimate latent slopes and intercepts when I run the full model with full constraints (variance and loadings to equality, with a marker item; intercepts and means to zero; unique variance to equality; unique covariances to zero), my fit statistics are very poor: 
CFI = .792; TLI = .802; RMSEA = .079; SRMR = .089

When I allow the residual covariance to be freely estimated, however, the model fit improves greatly:
CFI = .943, TLI = .941; RMSEA = .043; SRMR = .073


#1) How do I think about this? Do I use the fully constrained model, despite the poor fit statistics? Or do I free the constraints on my residual covariances? I'm not fully clear the conceptual (and interpretational) implications of choosing one or the other. I'm also uncertain about whether my model would converge with so many additional free parameters. 


#2) The 2nd part of my analyses entails a multivariate LGCM in which I'm examining the covariance between latent growth in the model above, and that of several other parallel processes. If one of these processes is specified with a model that is saturated or under-identified at t0, is it inappropriate to use that model in the LGCM? The fit indices of the saturated model across timepoints is as follows: CFI = .940; TLI = .948; RMSEA = .074; SRMR = .048.

My overarching goal is 1) to estimate linear growth of multiple latent factors across time, and 2) to estimate the correlation between their respective linear growth factors.

My understanding is that if my measurement model meets for strict invariance, I should constrain the residual variances (and covariances?) of the observed variables so that the variance and covariance is fully captured by the latent growth factors.
